newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt, futures hurt by spread profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: German debt, futures hurt by spread profit-taking.

text.p: German Bunds and futures were lower in morning dealings on Friday, hurt by profit-taking on spread trades and a weak U.S. debt market, traders said.
At 0750 GMT, DTB September Bund futures were down 15 basis points at 97.23 amid predictions the contract would be locked in a range from 97.20 to 97.50 for the session.
"The tone of the U.S. market is making it difficult for us to maintain these relatively high levels," one trader said.
Dealings were marked by unwinding of spreads by buying 10-year Bund futures against 5-year Bobls after the spread widened to near historic levels in recent days.
A half-day of trading in U.S. markets ahead of a long U.S. holiday weekend was expected to keep market interest limited.
No German economic data was scheduled for release, so the market was expected to focus on the release of the Chicago Purchasing Managers' Index at 1400 GMT.
On a technical basis, September Bunds should find support at 97.21, while resistance was pegged at 97.35 and 97.41 ahead of key resistance at 97.57, MMS International said.
"Recent failures to maintain above 98.00 is still a worrying factor," MMS said. "Selling upticks is favoured."
